history.summary: Shiva shrine at Bordubi, Tinsukia district, famous as the 'Bell Temple': devotees hang bells of bronze, brass, copper and aluminium (some up to ~50-55 kg) when their wishes are believed fulfilled - 'Tilinga' means bell in Assamese. Origin in 1965: tea-garden workers noticed a Shiva Linga emerging from the ground near a peepal/banyan tree; the garden administration built a small shrine around it. Bells were first tied to the sacred tree; iron frameworks were later installed to protect the tree. The temple has three bell-shaped domes and is reported in the Limca Book of Records for the largest collection of bells (verify). CSV town 'Tinsukia' is approximate - the actual site is Bordubi; reported distances from Tinsukia town vary across sources (7 km to 60 km, verify).

name: Tilinga Mandir
town_description: Bordubi is a small town in Tinsukia district of Upper Assam, near the oil town of Duliajan and surrounded by tea gardens. It is best known for the Tilinga Mandir, the bell temple of Lord Shiva.

travel.road: Bordubi is on SH-23; reachable by road from Tinsukia through tea-garden roads

visitor_information.best_time: February-May and October-November; Mondays are the busiest day
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-8:00 PM daily per travel guides; timings may vary on festivals
